<reason>CON won by keeping the motion as written and breaking PRO’s weighing. PRO’s best path was end-stage diabetes averted via earlier feedback, but CON forced the missing cutoff and then used PRO’s own concession that no outcome evidence ties consumer CGMs on non-diabetics to those complications. What remained—earlier lifestyle advice for patterns a normal A1c may not call disease—did not clearly beat immediate medicalization of meals. PRO’s symmetry/stakes argument had force, and both sides argued from mechanism, but CON answered the reach question (broader cheap screening) and made the comparison easier to decide. PRO’s clipped opening was a further execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s pressure questions on what reading counts as detection and what outcome shows consumer CGMs prevent amputation/dialysis, followed by PRO’s concession of no such trial and CON’s use of that collapse in weighing.</best_rebuttal>
